pattern.short_summary: The system derives a set of discrete terms, attributes, or dimensions from the material at hand and then puts that derived set on screen as the thing the user manipulates.
pattern.definition: The system derives a set of discrete terms, attributes, or dimensions from the material at hand and then puts that derived set on screen as the thing the user manipulates. The user steers subsequent behaviour by editing, weighting, selecting or deselecting members of the extracted set rather than by rewriting free text. The set is content-specific: a different input yields a different set of handles.
pattern.structural_signature: A derivation step produces a finite list of named items from the current input; those items are rendered as individually addressable widgets (chips, rows, sliders, editable fields); manipulating them re-parameterizes the downstream operation. The handle set is regenerated when the input changes, so the control panel's contents are data-dependent rather than fixed at design time.

dimension.category_description: How users, artifacts, examples, parameters, or user-state signals specify intent and shape the system's next behavior.
dimension.classification_boundary: Requires a user-facing specification or adaptive interaction; invisible sensing infrastructure is excluded.
